item.title: Lawmakers want upgrades to missing persons systems
item.description: Several state lawmakers are seeking a little more than $1.5 million for upgrades to New Mexico’s missing persons tracking and alert systems, along with two full-time employees in the Department of Public Safety for related work and a public awareness campaign about the Turquoise Alert system for missing Native people. item.title: New data shows patients struggling to access health care as providers consider leaving
item.description: A new statewide study adds fresh data to whether New Mexico has a healthcare workforce shortage, a question hanging over debates at the Legislature as lawmakers grapple with a number of policy changes to help the state keep medical professionals. item.title: Malpractice bill tangled up with concerns over private-equity
item.description: A bill to reform New Mexico’s medical malpractice laws was amended by a House committee last week to narrow its scope, sparking outrage among healthcare providers and confusion over who it would cover.
